title: Features of good citizenship
competency: List, show and acquire the features of good citizenship.

keywords.def: Living as a citizen who obeys the law, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic.
A set of rules made by a community that governs how people act and behave.
Taking action and doing your duties, like learning and reporting wrongdoing.
The ability and willingness to accept differences in ideas, beliefs and points of view.
Genuine love for your country and willingness to work and sacrifice for it.

ideas.name: What a good citizen is like

en.text: Nobody is born a good or a bad citizen. We learn good citizenship from our families, communities, friends and teachers. A good citizen respects others, helps others, listens to other opinions, lives in harmony with society, is willing to learn and knows his or her rights and responsibilities.

screens.title: Born or learned?
screens.ask: Is a person born a good citizen or a bad citizen?
opts: Neither: we learn to be good citizens
screens.after: Nobody is born good or bad. Families, communities, friends and teachers teach us good citizenship.

screens.title: 1.1.2 Features of good citizenship
paras: Nobody is born as either a good or a bad citizen.
Good citizenship is taught by our families, communities, friends and teachers.
table: A good citizen is someone who…
helps people who can't help themselves
lives in harmony with other members of society
is aware of his or her responsibilities and rights

screens.title: Case study: the award-winner
paras: At Parents' Day, a student won a special award.
The student followed the school rules and taught others to follow them.
He or she joined clubs and started an anti-corruption club.
The student lived in harmony with students of all ages, religions, languages and ethnic groups.
The student loves Ethiopia and won a woreda gold medal, hoping to raise the flag like Haile G/Selassie and Derartu Tulu.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Living as a citizen who obeys the law, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic.

screens.text: Tap the features of a good citizen.
screens.why: These are in the book's list. A good citizen helps people who can't help themselves.
screens.clue: One option is the opposite of helping.

screens.text: Is the student in the case study a good citizen?
opts: Yes: he or she obeys rules, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic
No: winning medals is not citizenship
screens.ans: Yes: he or she obeys rules, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic
screens.why: The story shows all four main features of a good citizen.

screens.text: Good citizenship is taught to us by our families, communities, friends and teachers.
screens.why: The book says this at the start of 1.1.2.

screens.text: Selam says: "I was born a bad citizen, so I cannot change." What would the book tell her?
opts: Nobody is born good or bad; she can learn good citizenship
Only teachers can be good citizens
screens.ans: Nobody is born good or bad; she can learn good citizenship
screens.why: The book says nobody is born a good or bad citizen. It is learned.

en.text: Obeying the law is one of the most important duties of a good citizen. A law is a set of rules made by a community. A good citizen follows rules, pays taxes, protects the environment and respects people. Responsibility means taking action: students learn, do homework, respect others and report wrongdoing like tax fraud or smuggling.

screens.title: Following rules
screens.ask: In the story, what was one of the award-winner's main contributions?
opts: Respecting the school's rules and regulations
screens.after: The student followed the school rules. Obeying the law is a key feature of a good citizen.

screens.title: A. Obey the law
paras: One of the most important public duties of a good citizen is to obey the law.
A law is a set of rules established by a community. It governs how people act and behave.
A good citizen obeys parents, teachers and people in authority, and upholds democratic principles.
A good citizen pays taxes, preserves the environment and treats people with respect.

screens.title: B. Responsibility
paras: Responsibility entails taking action.
One primary responsibility of students is to learn. Do your homework and respect classmates and teachers.
You must report wrongdoing, such as tax fraud and smuggling.
Keeping the environment clean, getting an education and community service are also responsibilities.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A set of rules made by a community that governs how people act and behave.
Taking action and doing your duties, like learning and reporting wrongdoing.

opts: A set of rules made by a community that governs how people act
screens.ans: A set of rules made by a community that governs how people act
screens.clue: Read the second sentence of "Obey the law".

screens.text: Tap the responsibilities of a good citizen.
screens.why: All four are in the book's list. Throwing rubbish breaks the duty to keep the environment clean.

screens.text: One of the primary responsibilities of students is to learn.
screens.clue: What is a student's main job?

screens.text: To be a good citizen one must be irresponsible.
screens.why: Responsibility is an important feature of good citizenship.

screens.text: Hiwot sees a shop selling smuggled goods. As a responsible citizen, what should she do?
opts: Buy them because they are cheap
Report it to the right authority
screens.ans: Report it to the right authority
screens.why: The book says a good citizen has a responsibility to report wrongdoing such as smuggling.
screens.clue: What does the book say about wrongdoing?

en.text: Tolerance lets us live peacefully. It means accepting that others may hold different opinions, beliefs and positions. A good citizen respects other religions, cultures and languages. Patriotism is genuine love for your country and taking part in its life. Patriots make sacrifices for their country, like the heroes of Adwa. Athletes, artists and other professionals who raise our flag are patriots too.

screens.title: Same or different?
screens.ask: Do you prefer friends who all speak your language and share your beliefs, or a mix of different people?
opts: A mix: we can learn from differences
screens.after: Diversity helps us learn and live in peace. Accepting differences is called tolerance.

screens.title: C. Tolerance
paras: Tolerance is a critical feature of a good citizen. It allows us to live peacefully.
It teaches us that others have the right to different opinions, beliefs and positions.
Tolerance is the ability and willingness to accommodate differences in ideas and points of view.
A good citizen respects other people's religions, cultures, languages and values.

screens.title: D. Patriotism
paras: A patriot has genuine affection for his or her country.
A patriot takes part in the country's social, political and economic life.
A good citizen is willing to make sacrifices for the country, like the patriots at the battle of Adwa.
Patriotism is also shown in diplomacy, education, medicine, agriculture, trade, art and sport.
screens.note: Athletes like Haile G/Selassie and Derartu Tulu raise our flag on the world stage. They are patriots too.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The ability and willingness to accept differences in ideas, beliefs and points of view.
Genuine love for your country and willingness to work and sacrifice for it.

screens.text: In a diverse society, ___ is important for peaceful coexistence.
screens.why: Tolerance allows us to live peacefully with people who are different.

screens.title: Tolerance or patriotism?
items: Working hard to raise Ethiopia's flag in sport
Listening to an opposite opinion calmly
A doctor serving people in a rural area to help Ethiopia
screens.why: Tolerance is about accepting others; patriotism is about loving and serving your country.
screens.clue: Is it about other people's differences, or about the country?

pool: Taking part in the country's social, political and economic life
Willingness to make sacrifices for the country
Putting personal gain above the country
a: Taking part in the country's social, political and economic life
Willingness to make sacrifices for the country
screens.why: These three are in the book. Putting personal gain first weakens patriotism.

screens.text: Patriotism can only be shown through military service.
screens.why: The book says patriotism can be shown in diplomacy, education, medicine, agriculture, trade, art and sport.
screens.clue: Read the paragraph after the Adwa picture.

screens.text: Chala is a farmer who uses new methods to grow more teff for the country. Abebe respects his neighbours of different religions. Which is true?
opts: Chala shows patriotism; Abebe shows tolerance
Chala shows tolerance; Abebe shows patriotism
Both show only obeying the law
screens.ans: Chala shows patriotism; Abebe shows tolerance
screens.why: Serving the country through agriculture is patriotism. Respecting different religions is tolerance.
screens.clue: Match each action to the feature it shows.

items.text: What do you understand from the story of the award-winner?
opts: A student who obeys rules, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic is admired as a good citizen
items.ans: A student who obeys rules, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic is admired as a good citizen
items.why: The book links the story to the four features.
items.clue: Why did everyone shout the student's name?

items.text: Which actions qualified the student for the award?
pool: Living in harmony with students of all religions and languages
Winning a woreda gold medal for the country's pride
a: Living in harmony with students of all religions and languages
Winning a woreda gold medal for the country's pride
items.why: All are in the story except copying.

items.text: How do you know whether you are a responsible student?
opts: Check: do I learn, do homework, respect others and report wrongdoing?
Ask if I am the tallest
items.ans: Check: do I learn, do homework, respect others and report wrongdoing?
items.why: These are the responsibilities in the book.
Putting personal gain above the country weakens patriotism.
items.clue: Which is the opposite of sacrifice?

items.text: What could increase Ethiopians' patriotic feelings?
opts: Teaching about heroes like those of Adwa and celebrating people who raise our flag
items.ans: Teaching about heroes like those of Adwa and celebrating people who raise our flag
items.why: The book praises the heroes of Adwa and athletes as a source of pride.

opts: Nobody; we are born with it
Our families, communities, friends and teachers
test.ans: Our families, communities, friends and teachers
test.why: The book says good citizenship is taught to us.

test.text: Which is NOT a feature of a good citizen?
opts: Is willing to make sacrifices for the country
Does not show respect towards others
test.ans: Does not show respect towards others

test.text: Tolerance means accepting only people who agree with you.
test.why: Tolerance means accepting different opinions and beliefs.

test.text: Reporting tax fraud is an example of which feature?
test.why: The book lists reporting wrongdoing under responsibility.

test.text: An Ethiopian artist shows the world our culture and flag. Which feature is this?
test.why: Artists who promote the country's name and flag are patriots.

notes.text: Case study p.8: "The school has also established trained to reward…" is garbled; read as "established a tradition to reward". Not quoted in the lesson.
Check-point questions that ask about the student personally (Are you responsible? Is diversity good?) are used as hooks or as multiple choice with book-based model answers.
Check-point p.15 Q2 (what weakens patriotism) is not answered in the book; the model answer (selfishness, corruption) is the opposite of the book's patriotic qualities.
